newsitem.title: EGYPT: Police shoot dead fugitive militant in south Egypt.
newsitem.headline: Police shoot dead fugitive militant in south Egypt.

text.p: Egyptian police shot dead a suspected Moslem militant accused of involvement in the massacre of 18 Greek tourists in April, security sources said on Monday.
They said the incident took place on Sunday when police went to Tahrir area in Beni Sueif province, south of Cairo, after being tipped off that Taha Yehiya Sayyed Hussein, 25, was hiding there.
Police in Beni Seuif said Hussein died after they returned his fire. They believe Hussein took part in the attack on the Europa hotel in Cairo in April in which 18 Greek tourists were shot dead.
The sources said Hussein was also alleged to have taken part in an armed robbery on a bank in Cairo as well as several other violent attacks.
In another incident, unidentified gunmen disguised as policemen shot dead a government employee in the province of Minya, south of Beni Sueif, security sources said.
They said Bahaa Sarawat Hassan, 32, was shot dead as he sat in his car on his way home on Sunday evening.
The identity of the gunmen was not known, but Moslem militants have been fighting a low-level guerrilla war against symbols of the government in Minya for several years.
The militants launched a bloody campaign in 1992 to overthrow the Egyptian government and set up a strict Islamic state. More than 1,000 people have been killed in political violence since.
